newsitem.title: LEBANON: Five killed in south Lebanon violence.
newsitem.headline: Five killed in south Lebanon violence.

text.p: A roadside bomb exploded in Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone on Thursday, killing a woman and her two children, pro-Israeli militia sources said.

The sources said the blast also seriously wounded the man who was driving the car carrying the victims. The bomb exploded near Markaba, a district capital in the eastern sector of the Israeli-held zone.
The attack brought the death toll this week in south Lebanon to 13 people -- five pro-Iranian Hizbollah fighters, one pro-Israeli militiaman and seven Lebanese civilians. Five died on Thursday alone.
The violence in south Lebanon, the last active Arab war front with Israel, raised concerns among Lebanese government officials.
Foreign Minister Faris Bouez accused Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of exporting domestic problems by carrying out attacks in south Lebanon.
Asked if he expected the violence to lead to war in the region, he told reporters: "We should expect everything."

Bouez said U.S. ambassador to Lebanon Richard Jones had telephoned him on Thursday and expressed the United States' concern over the situation in the south, site of frequent rocket attacks, clashes and roadside bombs.
Earlier in the day, a pro-Israeli Lebanese militiaman was killed in south Lebanon by a bomb planted in his car by pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas, South Lebanon Army (SLA) sources said.

In Beirut, a Hizbollah (Party of God) spokesman claimed responsibility for the bombing. That attack triggered heavy Israeli shelling which killed one Lebanese civilian and wounded two, security sources said.
Sheikh Nabeel Qaawook, Hizbollah's (Party of God) political leader in southern Lebanon, blamed the bombing that killed the mother and her two sons on Israeli forces.
"The Islamic resistance lays the blame for the crime in Markaba completely on the Israeli enemy," he said in a statement. "We warn the Israeli enemy against continuing this way."
On Tuesday, Hizbollah threatened to carry out suicide bombings inside Israel and Arab land occupied by the Jewish state.
It fired mortars and Katyusha rockets at the Israeli border overnight but no one was injured. Many residents of northern Israel spent a night in secure rooms and bomb shelters.
Israel set up the 15-km (nine-mile) occupation zone to protect its northern border from guerrillas. Hizbollah is fighting to drive the Israelis and their local militia allies from the zone.
Five members of the U.N. peacekeeping mission that has been based in south Lebanon since 1978 died on Wednesday night when their helicopter crashed. The cause was under investigation.

On Monday, Israeli commandos in helicopters backed by planes raided suspected Hizbollah targets in southern Lebanon. Five Hizbollah guerrillas were killed later by three roadside bombs planted by Israeli commandos.
